title: Bitcoin steadies amid technology weakness as portfolio value slips to $72,131
paragraphs: Bitcoin was nearly flat around $76,800, up 0.13% in Saxo's market update, while Ether slipped 0.04% to roughly $2,249. The broader tone remained defensive. Coinbase fell about 4% after an analyst downgrade, and Riot lost 7.6% as miners faced cuts to analyst targets. The Nasdaq 100 dropped 1.4% and entered correction territory, leaving crypto exposed to a wider retreat from technology risk.

The macro picture was mixed. Brent fell about 8% as renewed US-Iran negotiations raised hopes of easing energy supply pressures, while the US 10-year Treasury yield finished only slightly lower, near 4.91%. Cheaper oil could ease inflation pressure, but it did not produce a sustained recovery in risk appetite. US midterm elections and the coming employment report remain potential sources of volatility.

Strategy disclosed the purchase of 811 bitcoin for $65.5 million, taking its holdings to 849,327 BTC. Its filing also reported $208.2 million of STRC preferred-share repurchases, funded from cash. The company continues to add bitcoin, while allocating a larger sum to managing its financing instruments. That allocation matters when assessing how much corporate fundraising actually becomes incremental demand for BTC.

SEC staff added guidance on governance and network control to its crypto asset FAQs. Unaffiliated participants in broad-based governance generally are not treated as a controlling group solely because they take part in that governance, absent separate coordination. Unilateral powers to restrict access, change rules or reverse transactions remain relevant indicators of central oversight. This clarifies the staff's classification approach for token projects, although the guidance has no legal force and does not change the law.

Consensys introduced Sovereign Network Interoperability, software for coordinating securities settlement, currency payments and collateral transfers across institutional ledgers. The company says assets remain on their native networks, with cryptographic checks verifying cross-ledger execution. Ethereum-compatible chains are available; Canton connectivity is planned. The practical goal is to reduce the integration work banks face when connecting separate systems. Adoption and transaction volumes will determine its commercial significance.

Our two on-chain wallets total about $72,131: $11,852 in the active treasury and $60,279 in the cold-storage Safe. Combined value is $670 lower, or 0.92%, than the previous comparable observation. The Safe accounts for $538 of that decline. Its directly held 26.74 million ARC are unchanged in quantity and worth about $47,490, roughly 66% of the combined portfolio before ARC in liquidity pools. Its WETH/ARC pool adds another $9,873 of exposure to those two assets. ARC concentration remains the main portfolio risk.

Treasury Beefy positions total $2,270, down $44 in value, across ETH, AERO, bitcoin and other token pairs. Across both wallets, Aave holds about $7,739 of WETH collateral against $3,144 of USDC debt; health factors are 2.36 and 1.89, slightly below the previous readings. Fluid is only about $153 net, but its $1,063 debt and 1.03 health factor leave little liquidation headroom.
